significance.root_decision: For every even n >= 8 and every k >= 15, the polynomial F_{n,k}(q) = [n+k, k]_q - q^n [n+k-2, k-2]_q is symmetric of degree nk, has f_0 = f_1, and its coefficients increase strictly from f_1 up to the centre nk/2. This is Conjecture 3.3 of Chen and Jia in the setting of their definition (3.4), where n is even, which is also how the MathDB record states it. The proof works in the ring of semi-invariants of binary forms modulo the unique invariant Q of degree 2: that quotient is a domain, so the set of degrees in which a coefficient difference is positive is closed under addition; Sylvester's theorem identifies the differences with dimensions; uniform seeds in a few small degrees come from a quasipolynomial certificate for restricted partitions (3,632 residue cases, each a polynomial identity plus a sign check, with the coverage of all cases proved in Lean); a covering argument and a separate induction for n = 10 and 14 finish. Lean defines the Gaussian binomial as a sum over partitions in a box and proves the statement literally.
significance.caveat: Do not say 'resolves Conjecture 3.3' without 'for even n'. The source's definition (3.4) and the MathDB record restrict n to even, and the theorem proves that statement in full; but the conjecture's sentence does not repeat the restriction, the paper's example F_{5,9} has odd n, and the threshold k >= 15 is explained only by odd n, so the authors very probably meant both parities (the cross-model reviewer puts 0.25 on even-only being intended). For odd n with odd k the strict single-peak property fails by symmetry (for example F_{9,15}); with a central tie allowed the odd case holds numerically for n up to 41 and is open; nothing here applies to it. Computer-assisted: 364 of the 605 Lean modules are generated certificate data. The journal text of section 3 was not available. Cross-model confidence: mathematics 0.9, novelty 0.8, Lean statement equals the record 0.97.
